pages.text: The Crafting Terminal has four workspaces: the $(thing)Storage tab$() for stored items and typed resources, the $(thing)Craftable tab$() for recipes ready now, $(thing)Transform$() for explicit deterministic conversions, and the $(thing)Stations tab$() for installed processing and instant stations.

Transform keeps a searchable target list on the left. Insert one exact item into the visible upper slot, choose Auto to see all its uses or a produced target to filter them, then click one horizontal card. Each card shows its source inline; Auto never selects or executes a conversion.

Install the matching block on Stations, then select an output in Storage or Craftable. The preview shows the exact recipe, ingredients, station, process resource, Fuel, Mana, tool work, and output count. A neutral message appears when no supported recipe is available.

Use the shared ×1, ×8, ×64, or Max strip. Fixed amounts dim when the full batch cannot be made. Max checks ingredients, work resources, and destination room together and chooses the largest complete amount that currently fits.

Craft Output defaults to Player: results fill your inventory first and overflow returns to the Core. Choose Storage to send the complete batch to the Core. If every result and container remainder cannot fit, nothing is consumed.

EMI or JEI is the client recipe viewer. Either one is enough: the installed viewer may request the exact recipe shown by the terminal, sending its result to the chosen cursor or inventory destination. This remains one-level magic crafting: missing intermediates are not crafted recursively.

Craftable may show an output with zero stored quantity when its recipe can run now. Such an entry selects a recipe but is not a stored stack to extract. See $(l:auto_storage:recipe_costs)Recipe Costs and Support$() for station and recipe limits.

Stations has only Processing and Instant groups. Processing uses the larger area with item-overlay installed counts and separate accumulated-work values; Instant uses a compact icon grid. Their rows grow with the screen. Hover a cell for exact count, rate, and stored work.
